title: Negative: fuel-fed Cahn-Hilliard droplets whose catalyst is identity-carrying particles (pdrop) form from noise but arrest as a static emulsion: no division and no deaths in 11 settings
summary: pdrop replaces the catalyst fields of ad2-catalysts (threads/active-droplets) with Brownian catalyst particles that replicate inside droplet material and are reflected by a (c_new/c_old)^2 gate, as pcell did for phase_membrane. Started below the spinodal (phi0 -0.95 to -0.4) the particles die before any droplet forms; inside it (phi0 -0.3, noise 0.1, low particle death in the dilute phase) 56-122 droplets appear from a uniform soup within ~1000 t and then sit at a selected size: across fuel feed F 0.004-0.01 and fuel diffusivity Du 0.1-2 the droplet count drifts by <= 20% over 16000 steps with no growth-division cycle, and F 0.02 gives one domain-filling phase. The labkit pack (defaults: F 0.01, Du 0.3; 20000 steps) shows a packed static emulsion of ~100 droplets: 3 persistent splits against 26 merges, generation 1. This matches lab 1's ad0 result that 2D Zwicker droplets do not divide by shape instability; particle catalysts do not change it. Division in this family would need the core-starvation route of ad2 with large planted droplets, or a different growth law.
